_comment: Controlled glossary (termbase) for Ussher's Britannicarum Ecclesiarum Antiquitates. SEED — curate over time. Schema per entry: term (display), latin_pattern (IGNORECASE regex matched against segment Latin; word-boundaried, handles common inflections + ae/aelig), approved (list of acceptable English renderings), banned (renderings that must never appear), note (editor guidance). Lines without both 'term' and 'latin_pattern' are skipped, so this header is ignored.

note: Homograph. Default 'church' (the institution). Use 'congregation' only for a gathered body of believers.
Standard scholarly rendering is 'bishop'; 'overseer' is etymological but anachronistic here.
Render consistently as 'primacy'. 'Supremacy' imports a different juridical claim and would distort Ussher's argument.
Ecclesiastical vs. civil/legal sense both render 'jurisdiction'; editor confirms the domain in context.
7th-c Insular sense is closer to 'universal/orthodox', NOT the post-Tridentine confessional 'Roman Catholic'. Editor confirms sense per occurrence.
Keep distinct from synodus.
Keep distinct from concilium.
Homograph in Ussher's usage; 'presbyter' for the order, 'priest' where the sacerdotal sense is clear.
The ecclesiastical office, not the modern adjective.
Pattern excludes apostolicus ('apostolic').
Keep distinct from abbey/convent.
'pontifex Romanus' = Roman pontiff/pope; a bare pontifex may be an ordinary bishop in Insular/classical contexts. Editor confirms.
Homograph: ecclesiastical 'see' vs literal 'seat'. Beware Latin 'sed' = 'but' (a different word, not matched).
ch1 review (Alimaras): plural because Roman Hispania was divided into three provinces in Paul's time; rendering the plural as bare 'Spain' erases that. Singular Hispania may render 'Spain'.
ch1 review (Alimaras): keep the Latin form; 'Nepotian' is not a conventional English rendering.
ch1 review (Alimaras): one of the seven Apostolic Men of Spain; conventional English is Ctesiphon.
ch1 review (Alimaras): one of the seven Apostolic Men of Spain.
ch1 review (Alimaras): conventional English form is Orderic Vitalis.
ch1 review (Alimaras): Zaragoza is the better-known modern form.
ch1 review (Alimaras): render the epithet, do not transliterate it.
ch1 review (Alimaras): in Ussher pagan-idol contexts (Gildas on British idols) these are physical statues, so monstrosities not prodigies.
ch1 review (Alimaras): Tertullian's work; an 'apology' is a defence of Christianity. Render as the English title 'Apology', not a transliteration.
ch1 review (Alimaras): capitalize when naming a specific work (Jerome's Martyrology, the Roman Martyrology). Generic plurals stay lowercase.
ch1 review (Alimaras): 'usque' carries the sense of full extent; 'as far as' understates it.

banned: aliens from the commonwealth of Israel
strangers from the covenants of promise
note: KJV recitation. Ussher quotes the Vulgate; translate HIS Latin (e.g. "foreign to the commonwealth of Israel"). Caught verbatim in the ch1 draft.

banned: from the end of the heaven
note: KJV recitation that CONTRADICTS the Latin: "a summo caelo" = "from the HIGHEST heaven", but KJV Ps 19:6 reads "from the end of the heaven". The ch1 draft printed the KJV and inverted the sense.

banned: for a light to the Gentiles
note: KJV recitation. Translate the Vulgate: "that you may be a light for the nations".

banned: kept secret since the world began
note: KJV recitation. The Vulgate says the mystery was kept SILENT from the times of the ages; translate that.
KJV recitation. Translate the Latin ("at my first defence no one stood with me").
